These tests do not have it: they use yaml.safe_load, index jobs["queue"], and read the real `if:` and `run:` VALUES. 7. THE "SIBLING FIELD IGNORED BESIDE THE MATCHER" SHAPE IS HANDLED, not missed. `workflow_run: types: [completed]` fires for 'failure'/'cancelled'/'skipped' as readily as 'success'; the job reads the sibling `conclusion` field via `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`, and correctly exempts schedule/workflow_dispatch, which carry no conclusion at all. That exemption is necessary and right: without it the schedule sweep -- the self-heal this whole PR depends on -- would never run.

=== FINDING 1 (NOT NEW -- independently reproduced) ===

THE B1 GUARD IS WEAKER THAN ITS OWN DOCSTRING CLAIMS. I record this having found it independently before reading reviews/48/cloud-reviewer-clock-016Yb3Nh.json, which reports the identical measurement; I am not claiming it as a new find, and the convergence is itself mild evidence the finding is real.
test_auto_queue_enqueue_step_does_not_abort_the_loop_on_first_failure asserts only that each auto_queue.py-invoking line contains "||", plus that `exit "$rc"` appears somewhere. MEASURED: rewriting the loop body to

    LWB_PR_NUMBER="$pr" python scripts/cloud/auto_queue.py || true

leaves the ENTIRE suite green -- 611 passed. That variant never sets `rc`, so `exit "$rc"` always exits 0 and every per-PR failure is silently swallowed: the step reports success no matter how many enqueues failed. The docstring promises the test protects "while still failing the step overall if any PR errored"; it protects only the loop-continues half. This is the repository's own recurring defect shape -- a green result that cannot be distinguished from "I could not check" -- relocated into the guard for that shape. Suggested tightening: match `\|\|\s*rc=` rather than bare "||", or drive the real loop through `bash -e` against a stub.

=== FINDING 2 (I believe new) ===

THE CONCLUSION-GATE GUARD CANNOT TELL `==` FROM `!=`. test_auto_queue_job_skips_non_success_workflow_run_conclusions decides via `gates_conclusion(expr)`, which is three independent substring tests: "workflow_run" in expr, "conclusion" in expr, "success" in expr. MEASURED: inverting the shipped condition to

    if: github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'success'

leaves the ENTIRE suite green -- 611 passed. That inversion means the queue job runs ONLY when CI has FAILED and never when it has succeeded: the auto-queue would enqueue nothing, ever, again. Note what that is -- a green gate for a workflow that can never fire, which is on the explicit list of shapes this repository has already been burned by, and the exact class of defect (a trigger that had never once fired) that this PR chain exists to fix. Probe P5 shows the test catches DELETION of the guard; it does not catch INVERSION of it. Suggested tightening: assert on the parsed expression containing `conclusion == 'success'` as a unit, rather than three substrings that any expression mentioning those words satisfies.

=== OBSERVATIONS, RAISED NOT CHARGED ===

- The `concurrency` group falls back to `github.run_id` for the scheduled sweep, so two sweeps -- or a sweep and a workflow_run-triggered run -- can run concurrently against the same PR without serializing. The comment states this is deliberate. With a 15-minute cron and a 5-minute job timeout the window is small and a duplicate enqueue is idempotent at GitHub's end. Not charged.
- `resolve_pr_numbers`' schedule branch requests `pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=100` and does not paginate. At 12 open PRs today this is not live, but past 100 the sweep would silently truncate -- a "checked and found nothing" that is really "checked only the first 100". Not charged; flagged because the truncation would be silent.
- A `workflow_dispatch` with an EMPTY pr_number resolves to None and emits `prs=` (no sweep). The input is declared `required: true`, so this is consistent, but it does mean there is no manual way to trigger a full sweep. Behaviour, not defect.
- Neither the `workflow_run` nor the `schedule` trigger can fire until this lands on main -- Actions honours both only from the default branch -- so no CI run on this PR can demonstrate the trigger working. Inherent to the change, not a defect, but it means the "fired zero times" defect this chain exists to fix stays UNPROVEN in production until after merge. Someone should confirm a real firing afterwards.

=== A NEAR-MISS OF MY OWN, PRINTED AS REQUIRED ===

My first pass at deciding WHICH PRs needed review compared each existing record's `reviewed_commit` against the PR's RAW head sha, as my own instructions literally specify. By that test all 12 open PRs looked unreviewed, and I was about to re-review ten PRs whose code no reviewer had any outstanding question about. That test is wrong by construction: committing a review record ADVANCES the raw head, so a record can never name it. The gate itself does not work that way -- resolve_reviewable_head skips record-only commits -- and comparing against the REVIEWABLE head instead shows ten of the twelve are already reviewed at the code they contain. I caught this before writing anything. The cost of not catching it is visible in the repository: reviews/40/ holds SEVEN records and reviews/44/ holds FIVE, all naming the same reviewable head. I have reported this separately as a defect in the reviewer routine, not in any pull request.

The "touches a shared path and has 0 independent review(s)" failures are GONE -- this record satisfies REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS. So on the CURRENT main, a stale record VETOES an otherwise-sufficient set: adding a valid fresh review cannot clear the gate while any older record for the same PR remains stale, and a reviewer cannot delete those without writing outside reviews/<pr>/ in a way that would no longer be record-only. That is precisely the defect PR #54/#55 is titled for ("a stale review record must not veto an otherwise-sufficient set"). I am recording it here rather than silently leaving #48 red, because otherwise the next person sees a fresh AGREE and a red gate and reasonably concludes the review was wrong.

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: #48 cannot go green on today's main no matter how many correct reviews it receives. It needs #55 to land first (or the three superseded records removed). This is a finding about the MERGE ORDER, not about #48's own code, and it does not change my AGREE on the code.
